results.title: William Dobell
results.creator_credit: Dahl Collings, Geoffrey Collings and Collings Productions
results.brief_description: William Dobell has been acclaimed the greatest portrait and character painter of the twentieth century. The film with some 85 examples, reviews and interprets the artist’s work and development from his early days of struggle in London to his success in later times. This review of the work of Dobell includes not only some of his great portraits but also some examples of his early paintings. Suitable for upper secondary level.

results.title: Resistance and the 'High School Walkouts Against Racism'
results.creator_credit: Davina Rimmer, Markus Strazds and Misha Lamb
results.brief_description: The aims of resistance are to bring about a socially equal, democratic and ecologically sustainable socialist world and to organise, educate and mobilise young people to this end. Resistance, a Melbourne based organisation, was involved in organising high school students in protesting against One Nation and the racism this political party espoused and supported. This student movement was called “High School Walkouts Against Racism” and spread nationally with students participating in protest rallies outside the Queensland Parliament against Pauline Hanson and her One Nation Party. This short documentary presents personal views and commentary by two Resistance members, Andy and Liz along with actual footage of some of the protest rallies against racism. Soundtrack: Propagandhi and M.Y.C.

results.title: The Way of the Birds Storyboarding
results.credit_line: ACMI Collection, Sarah Watt Collection, Gift of the Watt-McInnes Family
results.brief_description:
Sarah Watt’s The Way of the Birds (2000) follows Maisie, a young girl whose fascination with birds transforms the way she sees the world. Like Watt herself, Maisie uses drawing to imagine places beyond everyday life, inviting us to see the world from new perspectives.
Trained as a fine artist, Watt made storyboarding central to her creative process. She used sketches to test ideas, shape emotion and gradually transform drawings into moving images. The storyboards, sketches and film stills on display trace that journey, revealing how imagined worlds first take shape on the page before coming to life on screen.
An award-winning Australian director, writer and animator, Watt embraced the expressive possibilities of drawing. Her hand-drawn films carry the warmth and immediacy of the artist’s hand, reminding us that animation is not simply about movement, but about transforming the way we see the world.

constellations_primary.name: Drawn worlds
constellations_primary.description: This Constellation follows artists who use animation to transform how we see the world. Moving between childhood imagination, fantasy and everyday life, these works show how drawings, silhouettes and sculpted figures can carry emotion and bring imagined worlds to life.
